candidates.exact_span: identifies the receiving stream segment no, 20.6.4.401(San Juan River (Navajo Nation boundary at Hogback to Animas River) is impaired for turbidity sedimentation/siltation and E. coli bacteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this discharge is within an impaired segment for turbidity/siltation and E. coli can affect which numeric limits are considered applicable and which parameter-specific monitoring obligations are in scope for FY2025 evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: NMED developed an EPA approved TMDL for the San Juan River Watershed (Part One)-Navajo Nation Boundary at the Hogback to Navajo Dam (May 10, 2005).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The geographic and watershed scope of the approved TMDL could change whether E. coli (and related) limits and monitoring derived from that TMDL apply to this facility's discharge point versus other river reaches.

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit proposes E. coli limits consistently with the approved TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting 'consistently with the approved TMDL' could change which enforceable E. coli numeric limits are selected for compliance comparison, whether E. coli monitoring is required for applicable periods, and how missing E. coli results are classified when TMDL-based expectations are disputed.

candidates.exact_span: The standard reopener language in the permit allows additional permit conditions if warranted by future changes and/or new TMDLs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reopener language makes the stated limit and monitoring set provisional or subject to supplementation could change which limits and monitoring requirements are treated as fixed for FY2025 versus left unresolved when future TMDL-driven changes are argued relevant.

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed draft are developed from the appropriate State WQS and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If 'developed from the appropriate State WQS' is read as the operative basis for limit and monitoring selection, a different reading of which WQS apply (State vs Navajo Nation, or which designated uses govern) could change applicable numeric limits and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: interim or final effluent limitations must be as stringent as those in the previous permit, unless material and substantial alterations or additions to the permitted facility occurred after permit issuance which justify the application of a less stringent effluent limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This antibacksliding rule and its facility-alteration exception could change which numeric limits are enforceable when comparing draft limits to the previous permit or when arguing that a revised limit is or is not justified.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed permit is slightly more restrictive than the previous permit since the Cyanide limits have been established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cyanide limits are newly established in the draft permit affects whether cyanide has an enforceable numeric limit for FY2025, whether cyanide monitoring is newly required, and how absent cyanide results are classified relative to prior permit terms.

candidates.exact_span: In addition, the 30-day average TDS net incremental increase and loading limits have been revised downward to 449 mg/L (from 497 mg/L) and to 24,992 lbs/day (from 27,664 lbs/day), respectively, in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These stated 30-day average concentration and loading values directly specify the TDS limits used for exceedance determination; interpreting 'net incremental increase' or which permit version governs FY2025 could change the applicable numeric thresholds.

candidates.exact_span: For other pollutants (i.e., BOD5, TSS, pH, E. coli, and TRC), their limits are kept the same.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This continuity statement affects whether FY2025 compliance uses prior-permit numeric limits for listed parameters and whether monitoring tied to those unchanged limits remains applicable rather than superseded by draft revisions.
